item.name: Sign and broadcast a Stellar tx via MPC

request.name: Sign and broadcast a Stellar tx via MPC

description.content:
Inspects the XDR against the sign guard (op allowlist, treasury source, destination whitelist, amount cap, fee ceiling), then signs through DFNS. A Soroban invocation passes in two cases only. One is a read-only view with no arguments and no authorization entries, on a contract listed in DFNS_SOROBAN_VIEW_CONTRACTS (our own factory when that is unset). The other is a vault deposit or withdraw_contract on a contract listed in DFNS_SOROBAN_TREASURY_CONTRACTS, and its first argument has to be the treasury, since that is the account the vault pulls from or pays back to. Anything else is refused. Fee-bump and restoreFootprint envelopes are refused too.
Success looks different depending on what you sent. DFNS broadcasts a classic tx itself, so that answer is {txHash}. A Soroban tx comes back as {signedTxXdr} for the caller to submit. If an approval policy is holding the request you get {pending: true, id} instead, and you poll /dfns/sign/{id}/status for the hash once it clears. Fail-closed: 503 when the API token, the wallet id, or the guard env is unset.

description.content: Backend for the Lobster dashboard. It wraps the DFNS custody service and a few reads. The custody routes are gated on an API token (LOBSTER_API_TOKEN); with no token set the gate is open for local dev. The DFNS reads answer 502 when the upstream call fails or the credentials are missing, and the sign path answers 503 until its env is in place. Creating a wallet, deciding an approval and paying a CCTP delivery also take the operator token (LOBSTER_OPERATOR_TOKEN), and stay shut until it is set.
